pr_title: Have OSSL_PARAM_allocate_from_text() fail on odd number of hex digits
pr_body:
The failure would be caught later on, so this went unnoticed, until someone
tried with just one hex digit, which was simply ignored.

Fixes #23373

issue_context.title: Inconsistent behavior for MAC hexkey of length 1
issue_context.body:
MAC key given in as a hexadecimal string of length 1 (e.g. `hexkey:F`) is treated the same as an empty key, instead of returning the "odd number of digits" error, as illustrated below:

* Digest produced using an empty key:

    ```
    ❯ openssl mac -digest SHA256 -macopt hexkey: -in /tmp/example.bin HMAC
    B167A8A891F4CA1032ECADF5854060E61A0AFEFDF7F61CE8D11FCAD8CD87D077
    ```

* Affected behavior – key of length 1 (digest is the same as above):

    ```
    ❯ openssl mac -digest SHA256 -macopt hexkey:F -in /tmp/example.bin HMAC
    B167A8A891F4CA1032ECADF5854060E61A0AFEFDF7F61CE8D11FCAD8CD87D077
    ```

* Expected behavior – as seen for a key of length 3 (or any $2n+1, n \geq 1$):

    ```
    ❯ openssl mac -digest SHA256 -macopt hexkey:FFF -in /tmp/example.bin HMAC
    Parameter error 'hexkey:FFF'
    40075A1ED07F0000:error:07800067:common libcrypto routines:hexstr2buf_sep:odd number of digits:../crypto/o_str.c:154:
    ```

Tested on OpenSSL 3.0.10 as shipped with Ubuntu 23.10:


comments: Yup, you're right, this is a bug.

Is it possible that this bug will cause the following error?

`Pending: 0008894BC87F0000:error:0A0003FC:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert bad record mac:../deps/openssl/openssl/ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1586:SSL alert number 20`

> Is it possible that this bug will cause the following error?

No. That's a TLS level error caused by some kind of corruption/problem when decrypting a TLS record.

review_comments:
Point is that the `TEST_` macros work a bit like assert(), and displays the expression that was tested if it doesn't return what the test macro expected.  It makes more immediate sense to me if it then displays that `OSSL_PARAM_allocate_from_text(...)` didn't return true, than if it displays that `result == expected` isn't true.

That is also a reason why I have an explicit `TEST_false()` alternative, because false is exactly what I expect in that case, and if `OSSL_PARAM_allocate_from_text()` returns true in that case, then that should be displayed as such.
